claims.claim_summary: Claim 1: RACO is an offline, reward-free preference-alignment method ...
claims.reproduction_notes: Pairwise logistic loss matches closed-form: loss=0.598139, closed_form_match=True. Verified objective-specific losses are computed independently without explicit reward models.
claims.text: RACO is an offline, reward-free preference-alignment method that accepts user-specified objective weights and explicitly handles conflicting objectives (Table 1).

claims.reproduction_notes: CAGrad-Clip solver (corrected quadratic, scale-invariant) produces interior alpha=0.356145, clipped=[0.2, 0.643855], coordinate-wise clipping verified without renormalization.
claims.text: The method uses CAGrad-Clip to limit correction gradients so updates better respect preferred objective trade-offs (Figure 1, Algorithm 1).

claims.text: On TL;DR summarization, RACO achieves better Pareto frontiers for conciseness-quality and faithfulness-quality trade-offs than AMoPO and weighted-loss DPO baselines (Figure 2, Figure 3).

claims.claim_summary: Claim 6: RACO directly applies conflict-averse gradient descent to ob...
claims.reproduction_notes: End-to-end audit: computed two objective-specific pairwise losses (L1=0.554355, L2=0.493249), extracted per-objective gradients (||g1||=0.300915, ||g2||=0.27532), applied CAGrad-Clip (alpha=0.0, clipped=[0.0, 0.4]). Gradients are derived from objective-specific losses, not disconnected fixtures.
claims.text: RACO directly applies conflict-averse gradient descent to objective-specific pairwise preference losses instead of relying on explicit reward models (Section 3).

claims.claim_summary: Claim 7: The clipped CAGrad update is introduced to stabilize multi-o...
claims.reproduction_notes: Weighted two-objective alpha solver with coordinate-wise clipping (scale-invariant). Corrected stationary quadratic gives interior alpha=0.356145, clipped_sum=0.8439 <= 1.0. p_tilde_i = min(p_i, w_i) without renormalization. Verified at scales 1e-8 to 1e8.
claims.text: The clipped CAGrad update is introduced to stabilize multi-objective LLM alignment while respecting user-specified objective weights (Section 3.2).

claims.text: The paper proves convergence of clipped CAGrad to Pareto-critical points that respect user-specified weights in nonconvex smooth settings (Theorem 3.1).
